subject: OpenLib \u0014 GitHub integration demo
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@openlib.org>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OpenLib - interest in GitHub integration

Hi Camila,

I signed up for Redwood yesterday after seeing your GitHub integration mention in the OpenLib docs. Really impressed so far - the latency and hosting model look promising for our CI pipeline. We're evaluating options to wire up a server-side agent that can comment on PRs with model-generated summaries and flag risky deps.

A couple quick questions before we book a demo:
- Does Redwood support installing as a GitHub App or do you recommend running via webhooks to a private runner?
- Any guidance on permissions (scopes) the app needs if we want read-only access to PRs and write comments?
- Are there examples for handling repo-scoped secrets / KMS integration for embeddings?

Would love to set up a short demo focused on the GitHub use case - ideally with a solutions engineer who can talk technical details. We're in the US Pacific time zone.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Engineering Lead, OpenLib
https://openlib.org

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@openlib.org>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-08-14T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OpenLib - interest in GitHub integration

Hi Jordan - thanks for signing up and for the great questions. I'm Camila on the SDR team at Redwood. Happy to coordinate a focused demo and bring a solutions engineer to cover the GitHub App/KMS details.

Short answers:
- We support both deployment patterns - GitHub App is the recommended path for tight integration and easier auth management.
- For commenting on PRs with summaries, read/write scopes for issues and pull_requests are typical; we can go through minimal-scope recommendations during the call.
- KMS integrations are supported on our Private/Dedicated plans; we can share a pattern for repo-scoped secrets and embedding encryption flow.

Would any of these times work for a 30-min slot (PT)?
- Today 3:00-3:30pm PT
- Tomorrow 10:00-10:30am PT
- Tomorrow 2:00-2:30pm PT

If none of those fit, feel free to pick a time on my calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/camila-30m

If helpful, I can loop in Alex (solutions engineering) to join the call. Also attaching a short pre-demo questionnaire - if you can share your primary repos and any example PRs we can tailor the walkthrough.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Quick context for the call so Alex can prep:
- Primary repo: https://github.com/openlib/openlib-repo (public for now)
- We're prototyping a bot that posts PR summaries and detects risky transitive dependencies.
- We currently store keys in GitHub Actions secrets and would like to discuss a more secure KMS flow - ideally something that doesn't require exposing raw API keys in CI logs.

I'm attaching a screenshot of a sample PR we want the model to summarize. Look forward to the call.

Cheers,
Jordan
